author: Contributor 87
about: Discord's published examples for the operations the discord pack serves (spec/doc-examples.json: its pages publish no example in the OpenAPI document). They are made by Mason, a developer building AIRHORN SOLUTIONS in his test server SomeTest from Discord's own pages: the OAuth2 page's code exchange, refresh and bot authorization, the current authorization, the Gateway Bot answer, the message page's request bodies and allowed-mentions cases, a reaction's rules and its object, a message's edit, the application-commands page's global commands (/blep, /permissions_test made twice) with their edit, list and delete, and the rules the pages state, each replayed as the refusal it causes. Two more applications he adds stand for a bot without a permission (Soundboard Lite, permissions 0) and one with only some (Mod Helper), which later fills its hundred global commands. Each setup step makes an example's precondition true or reads an example's effect; an example no World of this surface can set up is in notReplayed with why.

exampleDiffers.guild.roles[].permissions: The example predates API v8: a role's permissions are a string in the served v10 spec (role object, permissions: string) and on the permissions page ("Permissions are stored in a variable-length integer serialized into a string"); the integer is the older form.
exampleDiffers.guild.roles[].permissions_new: permissions_new was the string beside the integer before API v8 made permissions itself the string; the v10 role object (the permissions page's Role Structure, the served spec's role schema) has no permissions_new.
exampleDiffers.guild.system_channel_id: the guild the bot is added to was made in Discord's client (the World's guilds door, as a person creates a server), which gives it #general as its system channel; the published answer's guild has none set

notReplayed.oauth2_token#doc Client Credentials Toke: The client credentials grant is the twin's gap: no application of the demand and no step of the life asks for a bot owner's own token, so oauth2_token answers this grant as the twin answers what it does not serve (architecture, Creating a pack, step 7: an operation, or a variant of one, that only a published example reaches stays the gap).
notReplayed.oauth2_token#doc Webhook Token Response: The webhook.incoming authorization (a person picks a channel on the authorize page and the token answer carries the webhook it made) is the twin's gap: Cal.com's webhook, the demand's one, is made in its channel (create_webhook), and nothing of the demand or the life installs one through OAuth2, so the authorize page answers that scope as the gap.
